findings.title: Double interpolation of targets in sharded split path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on every non-hidden target, then build sub-requests via interpolateShardingSelector and passes them to runSplitQuery(). runSplitQuery() then calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again on the same targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). Because variables such as $__auto and $step have already been substituted on the first pass, the second pass is a no-op string scan over every expr/step for every shard sub-request. While idempotent, this is wasted work proportional to (number_of_subqueries × targets_per_subquery). Consider detecting already-interpolated queries or pushing the interpolation responsibility to a single layer so the work is done once.

findings.title: Brittle exact call-count assertion for applyTemplateVariables
findings.body: The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5). That count is tied to the current number of shard groups/requests produced by splitQueriesByStreamShard (currently 4 runSplitQuery sub-requests + 1 from runShardSplitQuery). Any future refactor that changes how shard groups are partitioned or merged - including the legitimate optimization of skipping the redundant second interpolation noted above - will break this test even when behavior is otherwise correct. Asserting on the final runQuery args, or checking the spy was called at least once per non-hidden target, would be more robust.

findings.title: querySupportsSplitting check now operates on already-interpolated expr
findings.body: applyTemplateVariables is called before querySupportsSplitting and partition. querySupportsSplitting() relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) returning true to keep $__range-bearing queries out of the split path (see the inline comment about backend interpolation with the split timeRange). Once $__range / $__range_s / $__range_ms have been substituted into numeric strings by applyTemplateVariables, isQueryWithRangeVariable can no longer recognise them and those queries will silently fall through into normalQueries and get split. The behavior change is benign for $__auto / $step but potentially incorrect for $__range queries, since the FRONTEND now substitutes them with the dashboard range while each sub-request still carries the chunk's range. Either guard the interpolation (skip applyTemplateVariables for queries that contain a $__range variable) or update querySupportsSplitting to detect the substituted form, and add a test covering a $__range expression.

findings.title: applyTemplateVariables mock mutates input instead of returning a new object
findings.body: The beforeEach mock for applyTemplateVariables does `query.expr = query.expr.replace(...); return query;`, i.e. it returns the SAME object reference with mutated fields. The real DataSource implementation in Grafana returns a fresh object via spread (`return { ...query, expr: ... }`), so the tests run against a fake implementation that mutates the caller's targets array. If someone fixes the mock to mirror the real implementation - or if the production code starts assuming the return is a new object - the test expectations (which look at the same query objects via runQuery mock.calls) can pass for the wrong reason. Recommend splitting the mock to return a new object so tests stay aligned with production semantics.
